_doc: Opponent pool registry. See TRAINING_PLAN.md for the full logic. Each member is a FROZEN checkpoint usable as a league opponent (ppo_trainer.py --pool-ckpts). GOAL: bias the pool toward HUMAN-LIKE opponents so the trained agent learns to beat humans. Add a member by appending to 'members' after measuring its humanness + strength. Paths are relative to ppo/. Load weights via torch.load(path)['model'] using the listed 'class'.
humanness_metric: BC top-1 match: fraction of held-out REAL human moves the model would make (greedy) on the same half-masked state. Higher = more human-like = preferred. Measure as train_bc.py reports 'val top1' over held-out human decisions.
selection_principle: Prefer high-humanness members; keep a few self-play members for variety. A new member is worth adding if it is MORE human-like OR genuinely different/stronger than existing members. Future: humanness-weighted sampling in collect() (see TRAINING_PLAN.md roadmap).

members.name: PPO_V4_init
members.notes: MOST human-like member. Weak standalone (overfits vs bots) but the ideal human-like opponent.

members.name: PPO_V6
members.notes: Human-like + has belief head. NOT yet loadable as a frozen pool opponent: 'v6' arch needs a policies.py adapter (see roadmap).

members.name: PPO_V4
members.humanness_basis: unmeasured (RL drifts from human style; measure before relying on it)
members.notes: Our best online policy base (V5 = this + uniform PIMC search, -3.78/round @50).

members.name: PPO_V3
members.notes: Kept for variety/robustness, not for humanness. Most consistent online (std 9).

members.name: PPO_V1
members.notes: Original self-play base. PPO_V2.pt is IDENTICAL weights (V2's strength was runtime search).

members.name: policy_all
members.humanness_basis: unmeasured (has play-history GRU context; not directly comparable to no-history val top1)
members.trained_on: human imitation, epoch 35 (checkpoint selected by best vs-OPPONENT-POOL score during training)
members.notes: WINNER of a 3-way checkpoint-selection experiment run this session, all identical data/arch/patience, differing ONLY in what training-time metric picked the checkpoint: online avg_score over 100 real games = -6.78 (this, vs-pool selection) vs -9.05 (policy_all_vs1, vs-Smart selection) vs -9.80 (policy_all_minloss, train-to-lowest-loss). CONCLUSION: selecting checkpoints by score vs a diverse opponent pool beats both vs-a-single-fixed-opponent and minimizing training loss -- use vs-pool selection for all future BC/RL checkpoint selection in this project.

members.name: policy_all_vs1
members.source: human-BC (ALL 1455-game corpus, same run as policy_all)
members.trained_on: human imitation, epoch 25 (checkpoint selected by best vs-SMART score during training -- old methodology, kept as the experiment's control group)
members.notes: Control group in the 3-way selection-criterion experiment (see policy_all). Online avg_score -9.05 over 99 real games -- worse than vs-pool selection (policy_all).

members.name: policy_all_minloss
members.source: human-BC (ALL 1455-game corpus, same run as policy_all)
members.trained_on: human imitation, epoch 55 (final epoch reached before patience-stop -- lowest training loss, not selected by any gameplay metric)
members.notes: Control group in the 3-way selection-criterion experiment (see policy_all). Online avg_score -9.80 over 100 real games -- the WORST of the three despite having the lowest training loss (confirms training loss is not a reliable proxy for online strength).

members.name: RL1
members.source: human-BC warm-start (policy_all) -> self-play PPO league vs the opponent pool
members.trained_on: 200 PPO updates (games-per-batch 64, learner-seats 2, snapshot-every 20 -> pool grew 21->30), checkpoint selected by best vs-pool score (upd 190, pool avg_score +0.38)
members.notes: First self-play RL iteration on top of the validated BC baseline. Local pool score barely moved vs policy_all's own (+0.38 vs +0.32). Online avg_score -7.53 over 100 real games, win_rate 6.0% (std 24) -- statistically indistinguishable from policy_all's -6.78 given the noise (SE ~2.4 at n=100). READ AS: 200 updates (~12.8k self-play games) wasn't enough training dosage to move the needle yet, not evidence the self-play approach failed -- the tiny local delta correctly predicted the tiny (noise-level) online delta, so the vs-pool local metric stayed well-calibrated here. Next iteration should scale up training (more updates and/or larger games-per-batch) before drawing conclusions about self-play's ceiling.

not_pool_opponents.name: BELIEF
not_pool_opponents.role: opponent-hand belief for SEARCH determinization (graft onto AlphaZero Big2ValueNet), NOT a pool opponent
not_pool_opponents.notes: 82.8% held-out P@count (chance 33%), 92-94% late-game. Ordering = clockwise-relative; convert to absolute-index when grafting.

runtime_modes_not_files.V2: PPO_V1.pt + 1s PIMC search at inference (no separate weights)
runtime_modes_not_files.V5: PPO_V4.pt + 1s uniform PIMC search at inference (best online so far)
runtime_modes_not_files.V6_online: PPO_V4.pt policy + BELIEF.pt belief-guided PIMC search (BELIEF=1; did NOT beat V5)
